Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The Afghanistan players are out in the middle. Paul Stirling and Kevin O'Brien will open the innings for Ireland. Naveen-ul-Haq will start the proceedings for Afghanistan.

Right then! 288 to win for Ireland. They need to bat well if they stand a chance of chasing it down. It won't be easy as Afghanistan have an excellent bowling attack and it promises to be an exciting run chase. Join us in a while to find out what happens.

Ireland's bowling was all about one man, Andy McBrine! He shone with the ball with a 5-fer and is the reason that they have managed to keep Afghanistan below 300. After starting poorly, Andy McBrine was given the ball and that worked as he picked up the first 5 wickets to fall and that had Afghanistan in all sorts of trouble. He was well supported by Simi Singh but the others proved to be very expensive. Curtis Campher was taken to the cleaners while Barry McCarthy had a disappointing outing. Overall, it was not a performance to be happy with.

Afghanistan were off to a brilliant start as Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Javed Ahmadi punched above their weight and stitched a 120-run stand. But once Ahmadi fell, the floodgates opened and they lost 5 wickets in a heap but Gurbaz continued and registered a century on ODI debut. He fell at the wrong time and then it looked like they will be restricted to a low score but Rashid Khan had other ideas as he flayed the bowlers to all parts of the ground and took them to 287. They should back themselves to defend this with the bowling line-up that they have.

66 from the last 5 overs has helped Afghanistan propel their score to 287 which is a very good one on this wicket. At the end of the 40th over, it looked unlikely that they will reach this score but Rashid Khan's blitz in the final five overs just turned things around. Brilliant stuff and they will be pretty pleased with the total in the end.

An appeal for LBW turned down! Good length ball on off and middle, Gurbaz looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal is made for LBW but the umpire shows no interest.
SIX! Bang! This is too short from Young and it is on middle, Gurbaz hammers it over deep square leg for a biggie.
Fullish ball on off, Gurbaz defends it to mid off.
FOUR! That is adding insult to injury Full delivery on off, Ahmadi lofts it over mid off for a boundary.

FOUR LEG BYES! The Irish players are not happy as they wanted the review but the umpires deny them becuase the 15 seconds were over. They are involved in an animated discussion with the umpire but nothing comes to fruition. Length delivery on middle, Ahmadi looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire denies it. The ball goes to the third man region for four leg byes. Ireland think of a review but but after a while, they want to take it but the umpire says no as the 15 seconds were over. The replays are shown later on and the Ball Tracker shows that it is umpire's call on hitting the stumps.

There is a long discussion going on between the Irish players and the two on-field umpires. Ireland want to review that LBW appeal but the on-field umpires suggest that the time was over to take the review. The Irish are not at all happy with that and are arguing with the umpire for that. In the end, they don't get the review and it has been signalled as four leg byes.

DROPPED? OR NOT? Yes, it a drop as it has come off the gloves. Poor stuff from Tucker! Short delivery down the leg side, Gurbaz looks to pull but misses it. It goes to the left of Tucker. Tucker moves to that side but fails to take it. A single taken.
Short delivery on middle, Ahmadi pulls it through square leg for a single.
Length delivery on off, Ahmadi defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length on middle, Ahmadi pushes it to mid-wicket.
Length delivery on middle, Gurbaz pushes it to mid on.
Full again on middle, Ahmadi flicks it through square leg for a run.

An appeal is made for LBW but it is turned down! Good length ball on the pads, Ahmadi looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. The Irish players put up an appeal for LBW but the umpire shakes his head.
FOUR! Swatted! Ahmadi joins in on the act now! Good start from Afghanistan so far. Short delivery on middle, Ahmadi swats it to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Full on middle, Gurbaz flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full delivery on off, Ahmadi looks to drive but gets an inside edge. It goes towards fine leg. The batsmen take a single.
Fuller on middle, Gurbaz tucks it to mid-wicket.
Full ball on off, Gurbaz defends it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Far too fine for the fine leg fielder. Gurbaz is off and running. Length ball on the pads, Gurbaz tickles it to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Gurbaz works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Lovely shot from Gurbaz! Shortish on middle and leg, Gurbaz pulls it to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Back of a length ball on off, Gurbaz defends it to cover.
Full ball down the leg side, Ahmadi looks to flick but it brushes his pads and goes to the keeper.
Fullish ball on off, Ahmadi defends it to cover-point.
On off, defended out.
Good length ball outside off, Ahmadi shoulders arms to it again.
Full ball outside off, Javed has no problems in leaving it alone.
Back of a length ball on off, Ahmadi pushes it to cover.
On a length outside off, left alone by Gurbaz.

EDGED AND FOUR! Just past second slip! Much better bowling from Barry McCarthy! Good length ball around off, Gurbaz looks to defend but it takes the outside edge which goes past Balbirnie at second slip. It races to the third man fence.
Good length ball on off, Gurbaz blocks it to cover.
SIX! Bang! What a way to open your account in ODI cricket! Sensational shot! Short ball on middle, Gurbaz stands tall and then hammers it over deep square leg for a maximum.
On a length on middle, Gurbaz stands tall and then tucks it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball on off, Gurbaz defends it to cover.
Fullish on off, Ahmadi prods on his front foot and then defends it to mid off.
Fullish ball outside off, Ahmadi drives it to cover.
Short ball around off, Ahmadi sways away from it.
Good length ball outside off, Javed makes a leave to this one.
Good length ball outside off, Javed pushes it to mid off.
Back of a length ball outside off, Ahmadi rocks on his back foot and then punches it through the cover-point region for a couple of runs.
Craig Young will bowl from the other end.
Just one from the first over. Fullish ball on off, Gurbaz pushes it to point.
Fullish ball on off, Gurbaz pushes it wide of mid off.
Fullish ball on middle, Gurbaz drives but finds the mid on fielder.
Full ball on middle, Gurbaz defends it back to the bowler.
Good ball from McCarthy! Very full on off, Gurbaz gets his bat down in time and then digs it out to the off side.
On a length outside off, Gurbaz watches it carefully and then leaves it alone.
Barry McCarthy starts off with a wide! Very full ball down the leg side, Gurbaz looks to flick but misses. Wided.

Right then! We are all set to begin! The Ireland players make their way out to the middle, followed by Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Javed Ahmadi. Barry McCarthy will start with the ball for Ireland. The sightscreen is not quite ready and there is a slight delay. Here we go...
Time for the National Anthems! Both the teams are out on the ground and are standing in respect of the respective National Anthems. Ireland's is up first, followed by Afghanistan's.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Kevin O'Brien, Andy Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Simi Singh, Gareth Delany, Andy McBrine, Barry McCarthy, Craig Young.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK) (ODI debut), Javed Ahmadi, Asghar Afghan (C), Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, Rahmat Shah, Azmatullah Omarzai (International debut), Rashid Khan, Naveen-ul-Haq, Mujeeb Ur Rahman.

Andy Balbirnie, Ireland skipper, says that it is a used surface and they would have also wanted to bat first but they don't mind bowling first. Adds that they had a good last game against UAE but they need to carry on the momentum.

Asghar Afghan, Afghanistan skipper, says they will bat first. Adds that it is a good surface to bat and they would look to put runs on the board. Adds that they have two debutants in this game and hopes that the spinners can do the job in the second innings.
Toss time - The conditions are lot clearer now and the toss is all set to happen. Up goes the coin and it lands in favour of Afghanistan. They have elected to bat first.

UPDATE 0952 local (0552 GMT) - The news out here is that it has become bright and sunny. The players have started warming up as well. Looks like the toss is not too far away. Stay with us for further updates.

Update 0935 local (0535 GMT) - Okay, here is some news for you! We are hearing that the toss has been delayed due to some heavy fog in Abu Dhabi. Let's hope that the fog clears and we get the toss and the action soon after that. Stay tuned for further updates.

Hello and a warm welcome to the first ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland in UAE! After some visa issues before this series, we are all set to see Afghanistan back in action after a long gap. Afghanistan have been a dominant force in recent times and they love playing against Ireland but some of their players might be rusty and that just might give an edge to the Irish in this game. Balbirnie's men are coming into this game after a terrific win over UAE, courtesy a fine performance from Simi Singh but Afghanistan will be a different challenge altogether. Who will come out on top? Will it be the Irish or will it be Afghanistan? Toss and team updates in a while.
